response: Multidisciplinary breast cancer clinics have been shown to be effective. Although planning and operating such clinics can be challenging, the benefits of this approach have been demonstrated. In these clinics, a team of healthcare professionals work together to make decisions about patient care, and the vast majority of these decisions are implemented. This multidisciplinary approach can lead to improved patient outcomes, as it allows for a more comprehensive and coordinated approach to care. Additionally, studies have found that the prognosis for patients with breast cancer has improved over time, suggesting that advances in treatment and care, such as those provided in multidisciplinary clinics, are having a positive impact. Overall, the evidence suggests that multidisciplinary breast cancer clinics can be an effective way to provide high-quality care to patients with breast cancer.
